readings.core_relation: Segmentation/COCO mean risks of 0.0987/0.0996 track 0.1; ImageNet loss 0.0499 tracks 0.05 while retaining leaf predictions, supporting graded-risk calibration without uniformly coarsening outputs.
readings.scope: Across 1,000 splits, individual risks can exceed target. Calibration sizes differ, confounding COCO's narrower distribution. Without monotonicity, risk can approach B; supremum-envelope repair requires other conditions and may be conservative.
readings.witness: predictions are almost always at leaf resolution.
readings.unclear: The other required repair conditions are not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Select the infimum parameter satisfying (n R_n(lambda)+B)/(n+1)<=alpha, using a safe terminal parameter if infeasible. Reserving B for the unseen loss makes this choice no smaller than a full-sample oracle, transferring its mean-loss bound to expected test loss.
readings.scope: Requires bounded, non-increasing, right-continuous, exchangeable losses and a safe terminal parameter. The guarantee averages over calibration and test observations, not a fixed calibration sample.
readings.witness: Including B makes the criterion dominate the mean loss

readings.core_relation: Conformal risk control extends binary coverage to graded expected-loss control by reserving B for an unseen observation; expected test loss is at most alpha.
readings.scope: Requires exchangeability, monotonicity, right-continuity, boundedness and a safe maximum; averages over calibration/test randomness. IID nonnegative losses without fixed-parameter jumps additionally give the sharp lower bound alpha-2B/(n+1). Without monotonicity risk can approach B. Four applications average near target across 1,000 splits.
readings.witness: boundedness alone cannot ensure risk control.

readings.core_relation: Conformal risk control adds the unseen-loss bound B to calibration losses, extending binary coverage calibration to graded expected loss with upper bound alpha.
readings.scope: Requires exchangeable, bounded, right-continuous, nonincreasing losses and a safe endpoint; averages over calibration/test data. IID nonnegative losses without fixed-parameter jumps have sharp lower bound alpha-2B/(n+1). Applications span 1,000 splits. Nonmonotonicity permits risk near B; upper envelopes restore control but may reduce informativeness.
readings.witness: a monotone upper envelope restores control but can sacrifice informativeness

readings.core_relation: Segmentation and COCO mean false-negative risks, 0.0987 and 0.0996, closely track target 0.1; segmentation's larger splitwise dispersion shows that near-target means do not guarantee each split or image.
readings.scope: Each uses 1,000 random splits; calibration/evaluation sizes are 1,000/781 and 4,000/1,000 respectively. Different tasks and calibration sizes confound dispersion attribution. The nonmonotone counterexample allows expected loss near B, preventing generalization beyond monotone losses.
readings.witness: the comparison does not isolate the effect of calibration size.

readings.core_relation: Adaptive conformal inference adjusts miscoverage using observed misses to widen sets, controlling accumulated errors under distribution shift. Average-frequency discrepancy is O(1/(gamma T)), not pointwise coverage.
readings.scope: Requires initialization in [0,1] and full/empty-set quantiles. Stationary hidden Markov bounds need fixed scores/quantiles and additional regularity. Volatility and constructed county ordering improve local coverage versus fixed calibration; unnormalized scores worsen swings. Step size trades responsiveness for volatility.
readings.witness: This controls long-run frequency, not coverage at every time.

readings.core_relation: After each response, update alpha_{t+1}=alpha_t+gamma(alpha-err_t); misses lower alpha_t and widen sets. Summation equates average excess miscoverage with bounded endpoint difference/(gamma T), controlling accumulated error pathwise without modeling shift.
readings.scope: Initialization in [0,1] and non-decreasing full/empty-set quantiles bound alpha_t in [-gamma,1+gamma]. Separate squared marginal-error bounds require stationary hidden Markov initialization, fixed scores/quantiles, Lipschitz statewise miscoverage and interior statewise target-attaining parameters; individual predictions are not certified.

readings.core_relation: Normalized-score adaptive calibration at step size 0.005 keeps 500-day volatility coverage near 90%, improving on fixed calibration despite shared GARCH refitting. Unnormalized scores cause wider adaptive swings. Adaptation avoids fixed-coverage troughs near county zone changes.
readings.scope: Volatility methods use 1,250-day fits/quantiles; four displayed stocks were selected for failures among twelve. County windows contain 300 observations, ordered by time zone with within-zone randomization. Supports tested local correction, not pointwise coverage or shorter intervals.
readings.witness: feedback did not remove sensitivity to score design.

readings.core_relation: Adaptive conformal inference uses each observed miss to lower miscoverage and enlarge sets. A bounded feedback recursion yields distribution-free finite-horizon accumulated-error control and long-run target miscoverage, beyond model/quantile refitting.
readings.scope: Not pointwise coverage. Hidden Markov concentration/marginal bounds require fixed scores/quantiles, stationary initialization and additional regularity. Volatility and ordered county examples improve local coverage; unnormalized scores worsen swings. Step size trades responsiveness against parameter volatility; outcomes are needed each step.
readings.witness: adaptation does not remove sensitivity to score design.
readings.unclear: Additional regularity conditions are not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Choose the smallest lambda satisfying [n R_n(lambda)+B]/(n+1)<=alpha, or a safe maximal parameter. Reserving the unseen-loss bound makes the chosen parameter no smaller than an all-sample oracle; monotonicity and exchangeability transfer the oracle's mean constraint to expected test loss.
readings.scope: Losses are bounded by B, monotone and right-continuous; the fallback must be safe. Expectation averages over calibration and test randomness, not a particular calibration sample.
readings.witness: the correction transfers a full-sample inequality to expected test loss

readings.core_relation: Adaptive conformal inference updates miscoverage after each outcome, widening sets after misses without modeling shift. Long-run miscoverage reaches target for any data sequence; experiments improve local coverage relative to fixed calibration.
readings.scope: Needs positive fixed step size and full/empty-set quantiles, not per-time coverage. Hidden Markov concentration/squared marginal-error bounds require joint stationarity, fixed scores/quantiles and additional regularity. Unnormalized volatility scores worsen swings; step size trades responsiveness for stability; each outcome is required.
readings.witness: This guarantee does not establish coverage at each time.
readings.unclear: Additional regularity assumptions are not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Update alpha_{t+1}=alpha_t+gamma(alpha-err_t) after each response; misses lower alpha_t and raise a fixed quantile threshold. Summation makes average excess miscoverage equal (alpha_1-alpha_{T+1})/(gamma T), so bounded parameters yield long-run target frequency without modeling shift.
readings.scope: Requires gamma>0, initialization in [0,1] and non-decreasing quantiles extended to full/empty sets, bounding alpha_t in [-gamma,1+gamma]. Extreme sets are allowed; individual or short-window coverage is not guaranteed.

readings.core_relation: Form sets at Q_t(1-alpha_t), then update alpha_{t+1}=alpha_t+gamma(alpha-err_t) after observing Y_t. Misses favor wider sets; coverage raises the parameter. Telescoping bounds frequency deviation by (max{alpha_1,1-alpha_1}+gamma)/(gamma T), regardless of the data process.
readings.scope: Requires gamma>0, alpha_1 in [0,1] and whole-space/empty-set quantile conventions; alpha_t stays in [-gamma,1+gamma] without clipping. Score/quantile functions may also update. Long-run control does not imply accuracy within each short window.
readings.witness: This operation calibrates the quantile argument

readings.core_relation: Conformal risk control extends binary coverage calibration to graded expected loss by reserving an unseen observation's worst-case contribution; expected test loss remains at most target.
readings.scope: Requires exchangeable, bounded, non-increasing, right-continuous losses and a safe terminal. IID nonnegative losses without fixed-parameter jumps have tight shortfall bound 2B/(n+1). Nonmonotone bounded losses can approach B; upper envelopes restore control but may be conservative. Four applications average near target across 1,000 splits.
readings.witness: identifying the loss structure on which its guarantee depends.

readings.core_relation: With normalized residuals and gamma=0.005, adaptive volatility coverage stays near 90% in centered 500-day windows, unlike fixed calibration despite identical GARCH refitting. Unnormalized scores worsen local swings; larger steps partly mitigate them but increase parameter volatility.
readings.scope: Both refit on 1,250 trading days. Four displayed stocks were selected for fixed-method failures from twelve, so panels show difficult cases, not average advantage. Cumulative frequency control does not guarantee local stability.
readings.witness: these panels illustrate difficult cases rather than estimate an average advantage.

readings.core_relation: Choose the smallest parameter satisfying [n R_n(lambda)+B]/(n+1)<=alpha, falling back to a safe endpoint. Reserving B upper-bounds the test-inclusive mean. The implementable parameter exceeds or equals an all-loss oracle, enabling finite-sample expected-loss control without calibrated model probabilities.
readings.scope: Requires bounded, exchangeable, right-continuous, nonincreasing losses and a safe endpoint. The guarantee concerns expectation rather than calibrated model probabilities.
readings.witness: rather than relying on calibrated model probabilities.

readings.core_relation: Adaptive volatility coverage stays near 90% in 500-day windows versus fixed calibration's departures despite both using 1,250-day GARCH/score refitting. Unnormalized residuals widen adaptive swings. Adaptation also avoids fixed-coverage dips at time-zone transitions in county prediction.
readings.scope: Four plotted stocks were chosen for fixed-method failures from twelve; favorable results for all twelve are reported. County coverage uses 300-county windows and randomized within-zone ordering, supporting constructed geographic drift, not election-night reporting performance.
readings.witness: adaptation to the constructed geographic drift

readings.core_relation: Segmentation and COCO mean false-negative risks of 0.0987 and 0.0996 track target 0.1 across 1,000 splits; their standard deviations, 0.0114 and 0.0052, show variation rather than per-split ceilings.
readings.scope: Calibration/evaluation sizes are 1,000/781 and 4,000/1,000; task/model differences confound attributing dispersion to calibration size. Without monotonicity, even losses in [0,B] can approach expected risk B. Monotone upper-envelope calibration restores control but may be conservative.
